machine: darwin arm64, node v22.22.0, Apple M4

summary.via: openai writer (callOpenAI) through OpenRouter's OpenAI-compatible API, model openai/gpt-5-mini, with reasoning_effort "minimal" added (as jevmem sends it to api.openai.com)

rows.input: I gave pdfkit a go for the invoice PDFs since WeasyPrint is slow on the big statements, but it needs wkhtmltopdf, which is archived and has no ARM build for our Graviton workers. Dropped it, WeasyPrint stays.
rows.line: Tried pdfkit for invoice PDFs but dropped it because it requires archived wkhtmltopdf with no ARM build for Graviton workers; stayed with WeasyPrint.

rows.input: I tried moving presence to the PG2 PubSub adapter to get rid of Redis. On Fly our nodes don't cluster reliably across regions, so people in Sydney showed as offline to everyone in Frankfurt. Redis is back.
rows.line: Moved presence to PG2 PubSub adapter to remove Redis but failed because Fly nodes don't cluster reliably across regions (Sydney seen offline from Frankfurt); reverted to Redis.

rows.input: Swapped Jason for OTP 27's built-in json module to cut a dependency. It orders map keys differently, and a few hundred snapshot tests on the event payloads broke. Not worth the churn, back to Jason.
rows.line: Swapped Jason for OTP 27 built-in json to cut dependency; it orders map keys differently causing hundreds of snapshot test failures, reverted back to Jason.

rows.input: I tried serving the tiles with Martin instead of our Fastify app so we could delete the layer SQL files. Martin can't call our per-zoom SQL functions with the extra filter parameters, and half the layers need them. We stay on our own server.
rows.line: Served tiles with Martin instead of our Fastify app but failed because Martin can't call our per-zoom SQL functions with extra filter parameters needed by half the layers; we stay on our server

rows.input: Brotli at the origin was a dud: the CDN re-compresses whatever it caches with its own gzip, so the brotli work only burned CPU on the origin. Turned it off.
rows.line: Enabled Brotli compression on origin was a dud because CDN re-compresses cached assets with its own gzip, wasting origin CPU; Brotli was turned off.

rows.input: Tried AVAudioEngine for variable speed to get better pitch correction. It won't play the HLS streams that some feeds use, only local files, so I dropped it and kept AVPlayer's timePitchAlgorithm.
rows.line: AVAudioEngine for variable speed failed because it doesn't play HLS streams (only local files); dropped in favor of AVPlayer with its timePitchAlgorithm.

rows.input: I tested SwiftData as a replacement for Core Data on a branch. Migrating our existing store crashed on the episode-to-chapters relationship, and SwiftData has no way to write a custom mapping model. Staying on Core Data.
rows.line: Tested SwiftData as Core Data replacement; migrating existing store crashed on episode-to-chapters relationship and SwiftData lacks custom mapping model support; stayed on Core Data

rows.input: I tried putting the MQTT client on esp-mqtt through the C bindings instead of rust-mqtt, hoping for better reconnects. The binding dragged in the whole ESP-IDF networking stack and the image came out at 2.1 MB, over the OTA partition, so I dropped it.
rows.line: Putting MQTT client on esp-mqtt via C bindings dragged in entire ESP-IDF networking stack, produced 2.1MB image exceeding OTA partition, so dropped that approach (kept rust-mqtt).

rows.input: fwiw we tried HTMX for the reconciliation screen. matching 500 transactions needs a lot of client-side state (drag to match, undo), and every interaction was a server round trip, it felt laggy on the accountants' laptops. went back to the React widget for that screen only.
rows.line: Used HTMX for reconciliation screen but it felt laggy because matching 500 transactions required heavy client-side state and every interaction was a server round trip; reverted to React widget.

rows.input: I tried running the per-account fetches in a Celery group so they go out in parallel. The aggregator started answering 429 once more than 4 requests per client ID were in flight, and the retries made the whole sync slower (26 minutes). I reverted to sequential fetches; incremental sync with the since parameter is probably the real fix.
rows.line: Ran per-account fetches in a Celery group; aggregator returned 429 when >4 requests per client ID were in flight and retries slowed sync to 26min; reverted to sequential fetches; incremental sync…

rows.input: I tried LiveView's chunked uploads with a bigger chunk size, but a reconnect creates a new upload entry and throws away the chunks already sent; the protocol has no resume. I left uploads as they were. Resumable uploads would need tus or S3 multipart directly.
rows.line: LiveView chunked uploads with larger chunk size failed because reconnect creates new upload and discards previous chunks (no resume); kept original uploads; resumable needs tus or S3 multipart…

rows.input: I tried light sleep between the 10 s samples. The Wi-Fi association dropped on every wake with the router's DTIM setting, and reconnecting cost more than the sleep saved: average draw went up to 0.62 W from 0.55 W. I reverted it.
rows.line: Used light-sleep between 10 s samples; Wi‑Fi association dropped on every wake due to router DTIM causing reconnect overhead, increasing avg draw 0.62W vs 0.55W, so reverted.

rows.input: I tried replacing the List with a LazyVStack inside a ScrollView. Scrolling was smoother at first, but memory grew without bound because LazyVStack never releases rows that scrolled away, and a 3,000-episode feed hit 900 MB. I put the List back; the stutter comes from decoding artwork on the main thread, which I'll look at next.
rows.line: Replaced List with ScrollView+LazyVStack; initial smoother scroll but memory grew without bound because LazyVStack didn't release offscreen rows, 3,000 items hit ~900MB; reverted to List; stutter…

rows.input: I tried a materialized view of the parcels simplified per zoom. Generation got faster, but refreshing the view takes 40 minutes and blocks reads unless it's CONCURRENTLY, which needs a unique index the table can't have (parcel IDs repeat across counties). I dropped it.
rows.line: Created a materialized view for parcels simplified per zoom; generation faster but REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW blocks reads and takes 40 min; CONCURRENTLY impossible due to non-unique parcel IDs across…

rows.input: The VAT returns were drifting by a penny. Quantizing with Decimal on every line didn't fix it, totals were still off by 1p on some returns. Rounding once on the return total, the way HMRC does, fixed all of them.
rows.line: VAT returns drifted by 1p; quantizing each line with Decimal didn't fix it; rounding once on the return total (HMRC method) fixed the issue.

rows.input: I first tried sorting by inserted_at in the LiveView, but the nodes' clocks differ by up to 80 ms, so messages still jumped around. I added a per-room sequence number from Postgres and sort by that now; the ordering test passes.
rows.line: Sorted by inserted_at in LiveView failed because node clocks differed up to 80ms causing jumps; added per-room sequence number from Postgres and now sort by that; ordering test passes

rows.input: I tried ST_Simplify with a 2 m tolerance before ST_AsMVT. The tiles got smaller, but neighbouring buildings started to overlap and small ones collapsed into slivers the style can't draw cleanly, so I reverted it. Dropping the height attribute below z15 took the worst tile from 640 KB to 470 KB instead.
rows.line: Used ST_Simplify 2m before ST_AsMVT; produced smaller tiles but caused neighboring buildings to overlap and small buildings collapse into slivers so reverted; dropping height attr <z15 reduced worst…

rows.input: The CDN kept serving stale tiles after data updates. Purging by URL prefix did nothing because the CDN only purges exact URLs. Tagging responses with a Surrogate-Key per layer and purging the tag clears them in seconds.
rows.line: CDN served stale tiles after updates because purging by URL prefix failed (CDN purges exact URLs only); switched to Surrogate-Key per layer and purging tags clears tiles in seconds

rows.input: I first tried keeping the download task alive with a background task identifier, but iOS still suspends it after about 30 seconds. A background URLSession configuration hands the downloads to the system instead, and they finish with the app suspended now.
rows.line: Keeping the download task alive with a background task identifier, but iOS still suspends it after about 30 seconds.
rows.fellBack: the LLM's line gave no reason (or was empty)

rows.input: Chapter images were blurry on the lock screen. Giving MPMediaItemArtwork a bigger bounds size changed nothing, the system kept using the 300 px thumbnail from the feed. Downloading the full-size chapter image and handing that over fixed it.
rows.line: Chapter images were blurry on lock screen because iOS ignored larger MPMediaItemArtwork bounds and used 300px feed thumbnail; downloading and supplying full-size chapter image fixed it

rows.input: I first recalibrated the HLW8012 with a new resistor ratio, but the drift was back after two hours: it's temperature, the chip warms up next to the relay. Applying the datasheet's temperature compensation from the onboard sensor keeps readings within 1% over 12 hours.
rows.line: Recalibrated HLW8012 with new resistor ratio but readings drifted after ~2 hours due to chip warming near relay; applying datasheet temperature compensation from onboard sensor keeps readings within…

rows.input: WeasyPrint has been a pain for months: a 40-page statement takes 25 s and times out the request, and its system libraries keep breaking the Docker build. Invoice PDFs move to Typst, which renders the same statement in under a second.
rows.line: WeasyPrint was abandoned after 40-page PDFs took ~25s and caused request timeouts and Docker build breakages; invoices moved to Typst which renders same statement in <1s.

rows.input: Presigned uploads straight to S3 haven't worked for the enterprise customers: their proxies block amazonaws.com, so uploads fail for whole companies. Uploads go through our own endpoint from now on.
rows.line: Presigned S3 uploads failed for enterprise customers because their proxies block amazonaws.com; switched to routing uploads through our own endpoint instead

rows.input: Serving the styles from the tile origin didn't hold up: every style tweak needed a tile server deploy, and a bad deploy took the styles down with the tiles twice this month. Styles move to a static bucket behind the CDN.
rows.line: Serving styles from tile origin failed because each tweak required tile-server deploys and bad deploys took styles down twice this month; styles moved to static bucket behind CDN

rows.input: Refreshing feeds in BGAppRefreshTask hasn't worked out: iOS runs it maybe twice a day for most users, so new episodes show up hours late. Refresh moves to our server, which sends a silent push when a feed changes.
rows.line: Refreshing feeds in BGAppRefreshTask failed because iOS schedules it ~twice/day causing late episodes; moved refresh to server which sends silent push on feed change.

rows.input: Pulling OTA images over HTTPS on each device didn't work in practice: the TLS handshake needs about 40 KB of heap the metering task can't spare, and devices ran out of memory mid-download. We're switching to pushing the image over MQTT in chunks, still ed25519-signed.
rows.line: Pulling OTA images over HTTPS failed because TLS handshake required ~40KB heap the metering task couldn't spare causing OOM; switched to pushing image over MQTT in chunks with ed25519 signatures
